summary: A first-person feature in The Age collects stories of adults who moved back in with their parents amid money, housing and life pressures. Alexandra, 37, lived with her parents after heartbreak and again after her son's birth; Tess Moone and her husband Dane got stuck with his parents after selling their Perth home; and photographer Rachel Claire moved home in 2019 for financial reasons. Each describes both the support and the loss of independence that come with it.
one_line: Three adults describe moving back in with their parents, weighing the financial and emotional support against lost independence and privacy.
key_facts: Alexandra, 37, stayed with her parents for four months before moving out to house-sit a friend's place.
After fertility treatment alone, Alexandra became pregnant and had found a stable job and rented an apartment before the birth.
After her son was born, Alexandra moved back in with her parents for the first three months of his life.
Alexandra wrote a memoir, Inconceivable, about becoming a solo mum and moving back in with her parents in her late 30s.
Tess Moone, a 31-year-old travel writer, and her husband Dane became home owners at age 21, buying a house 10 minutes from Perth's CBD.
Tess and Dane sold their Perth home in February and spent six months travelling around Europe and Japan, intending to move to Margaret River.
They expected to stay with Dane's parents for three to four weeks, but the stay has stretched out month after month because of the Margaret River rental crisis.
Landlords prefer to rent to families or people who have rented before, so Tess and Dane keep getting knocked back despite offering more than the asking price or more rent upfront.
Tess and Dane agreed to move into a friend's holiday home sight unseen, but must return to Dane's parents when the friend wants to use it, such as at Christmas.
Tess says that if they had known then what they know now, they'd never have sold their home.
Rachel Claire, a 32-year-old photographer, moved back in with her parents in 2019 because of job insecurity and financial practicality.
Rachel first moved out at 22; she moved back home so she could travel for work with minimal financial impact, and cited her parents' home security systems as a benefit for her expensive gear.
